passage: Sofia had until the last day of March to choose between the science track and the arts track at her school in Lisbon. In October she said she would wait for a sign. In December she was still waiting. In February her friend Jin signed up for the arts choir, and the science club's summer lab filled up. Sofia lay awake with a tight stomach, checking her phone for someone to decide for her. Two weeks before the deadline she wrote two columns on paper: what she knew, and what she could not know. There was still no sign, and there were fewer choices than in October. She chose science and told her mother.

qa.q: When was the deadline for choosing a track?
qa.a: The deadline was the last day of March.

qa.q: What was Sofia feeling as she lay awake in February?
qa.a: Sofia felt anxious, with a tight stomach, hoping that someone or something would decide for her.

qa.q: What did Sofia do at the two-week mark that helped?
qa.a: She wrote two columns, what she knew and what she could not know, then made a choice and told her mother.

qa.q: How might Jin see Sofia's waiting?
qa.a: Jin, who had already signed up for the choir, might see waiting as safe, without noticing that places were filling up around Sofia.

grounding: Shows a teenager delaying a stream choice for months hoping for a clear sign while options narrow and anxiety grows.

passage: Charu kept the Class 10 stream form in her bag for three weeks. Every day she told herself she would fill it in when she felt sure. On the last Monday it was still blank, and Vandana ma'am, the school counsellor, called her in. "Not sure yet," Charu said, picking at her nails. The commerce batch was already full and only two seats remained in science, but the form needed one choice by evening. "I'm scared of picking wrong," she said. Vandana ma'am asked what Charu had learned about each stream so far. Charu counted on her fingers and was surprised that the list was longer than she thought. She ticked a box before the bell.

qa.q: How long did Charu keep the form in her bag?
qa.a: Charu kept the form in her bag for three weeks.

qa.q: Why did Charu pick at her nails when she said "Not sure yet"?
qa.a: Charu was nervous and afraid of picking wrong, and waiting to feel sure had not made the fear go away.

qa.q: What small step helped Charu move from waiting to choosing?
qa.a: She counted what she had learned about each stream and saw the list was longer than she thought, then ticked a box.

qa.q: How does Vandana ma'am see Charu's blank form?
qa.a: Vandana ma'am sees a student who is scared, and asks what Charu already knows instead of telling her what to choose.

grounding: Shows a teenager waiting for certainty about a stream while choices shrink and worry grows.

passage:
Dear Aparna didi,

You asked if I've chosen my stream for Class 11. I haven't. Science because I like biology? Commerce because Papa says it's practical? Arts because I love history? I keep waiting to wake up one morning and just know.

It's been since October. Now the form is due in two weeks, and the commerce seats at my school are already full. So I've lost one option by waiting. My stomach hurts every time Mummy asks.

Maybe there isn't a perfect sign. Maybe I just have to pick the one I'd be least sorry about. Can we talk on Sunday? I need to decide.

Lalit

qa.q: Which option has Lalit already lost by waiting?
qa.a: The commerce seats at the school are already full.

qa.q: How does Lalit feel each time Mummy asks about the stream?
qa.a: Lalit feels anxious, with a stomach ache, because the decision keeps being postponed.

qa.q: What could help Lalit decide on Sunday?
qa.a: Talking it through with Aparna didi and choosing the stream Lalit would be least sorry about, instead of waiting for certainty.

qa.q: How might Aparna didi feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Aparna didi might feel concerned but glad that Lalit is asking for help before the form is due.

grounding: A teenager's letter shows months of waiting for a clear sign about which stream to choose, while options narrow and anxiety grows.

passage: You want to hear how I nearly missed choosing my college? I'm Zainab. In Class Twelve I got into two courses: psychology in Pune and nursing in Mumbai. I kept waiting to feel sure. I'd make lists, ask aunties, watch videos, and still feel fifty-fifty. My friend Aditi chose her course in a week and teased me. "You'll be deciding till you're forty." The Pune college gave a deadline. I let it pass, still hoping for a sign. Then Mumbai filled up too, and I had to take a waitlist spot at a third college I hadn't even wanted. That year I learned certainty doesn't come on time. You pick, and then you make the choice good.

qa.q: Which two courses did Zainab get into?
qa.a: Psychology in Pune and nursing in Mumbai.

qa.q: How did Zainab feel while waiting to be sure?
qa.a: Zainab felt torn and anxious, still fifty-fifty despite lists, advice and videos.

qa.q: What lesson did Zainab draw from losing both options?
qa.a: That certainty rarely arrives on time, so it is better to pick and then make the choice good.

qa.q: How might Aditi see Zainab's long wait?
qa.a: Aditi, who chose in a week, found it frustrating and teased Zainab, perhaps worried about the deadlines.

grounding: A young adult recalls waiting for certainty about a course until the waiting itself closed both options.

passage:
September. Uday, sixteen, had to choose between science and commerce by December. He liked physics but loved business news. "I'll wait till I feel sure," he told his cousin Farhan.
November. He still wasn't sure. He'd started losing sleep. His school announced that the science section had only five seats left. He froze and did nothing.
Early December. The science seats were gone. Only commerce remained. Farhan sat with him. "Would you have been happy in commerce anyway?" Uday thought, surprised. "Actually... yes." Farhan said, "Then choose it for real, not because it's all that's left." Uday filled in the form that evening, relieved and a little sad about the months he'd lost worrying.

qa.q: How many science seats were left in November?
qa.a: The science section had only five seats left.

qa.q: How did Uday feel in November?
qa.a: He felt anxious and frozen, losing sleep and unable to act.

qa.q: What did Farhan's question help Uday do?
qa.a: It helped Uday see he could be happy in commerce and choose it for real rather than by default.

qa.q: How might Farhan have felt watching Uday wait?
qa.a: Farhan likely felt worried and a little frustrated, seeing Uday lose options and sleep by waiting to feel sure.

grounding: Shows over months a teenager waiting for certainty about a stream while options narrow and anxiety rises.

passage: "Ojas, you keep saying you'll pick your stream when you're sure. Let me, your Tarun chacha, tell you about my summer of waiting to be sure. I was sixteen. The choice was the polytechnic in Nashik for electrical, or commerce at the local college. I wanted a sign. I asked my teacher, then the astrologer uncle next door, then I waited for my board result to decide for me. It came, good marks, and still no sign. My friend Sandeep filled his form in May and kept saying, 'Just choose, you can change later.' I kept waiting. By the time I went to Nashik in July, electrical was full. I took mechanical, the only seat left, and spent two years with a knot in my stomach every morning. Not because the choice was wrong. Because I never actually made it."

qa.q: Which course did young Tarun end up taking?
qa.a: Mechanical, the only seat left.

qa.q: What was young Tarun feeling through that summer?
qa.a: He was anxious and unsure, wanting a clear sign before choosing, and later felt a knot in his stomach every morning.

qa.q: What could young Tarun have done in May, when Sandeep filled his form?
qa.a: He could have picked the option that seemed best so far and applied, knowing he could change later, instead of waiting for certainty.

qa.q: How might Sandeep have seen Tarun's waiting that summer?
qa.a: Sandeep was probably puzzled and a bit worried, seeing that waiting was costing more than a choice would, which is why he kept saying "just choose".

grounding: Shows a teenager who waits months for certainty about a course, and the waiting narrows his options and adds to his worry.
